questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. He meets me in the same frank friendly way as always without mentioning it.

B. He has owed it to me for twelve months now.

C. I can realise whenever I meet him that he has forgotten that he owes me a dollar.

D. My friend Todd owes me a dollar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. **DBCA**.

The sentence can not start with A and B because it is starting with a pronoun.

Sentence C is also talking about ( HIM) and we have to find the noun used for the HIM.

So sentence can start only with the D because it contains the Noun about which the sentence is talking.

So, the correct arrangement is **DBCA**.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

On Saturday Rahul visited his professor to whom he had an appointment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e.** to whom he had.**

Appointment can be followed by multiple prepositions.

Eg: 1) I have an appointment **with **Ram. 

 2) I gave an appointment **to **Radha. 

 3) Please schedule an appointment **for **tomorrow. 

We have to use here **with **instead of to** **for making the sentence correct, since **to **is used when an appointment is **given to someone**.

The correct sentence will be- **On Saturday Rahul visited his professor with whom he had an appointment.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The given sentence is in past tense so option 1 cannot be the answer as it is in present tense.
 
• If the active sentence is in past tense, was/were will be used in its passive form therefore, option 2 cannot be the answer.
 
• Option 4 cannot be the answer because the subject and object have been interchanged. 
 
• Therefore, the only option that satisfies the condition is Option 2.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The stranger said to me, "Can you tell me the way to the River Bank Colony?"

options.text: The stranger asked me if you could tell him the way to the River Bank Colony.
The stranger told me that I could tell him the way to the River Bank Colony.
The stranger asked me can you tell me the way to the River Bank Colony.
The stranger asked me if I could tell him the way to the River Bank Colony.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• Given an active sentence is in interrogative form therefore interrogative will be changed to an assertive sentence. To change the sentence into an indirect sentence,** a sentence in the present tense, change it into the corresponding past tense.**
 
• **'Said to'** will be changed to '**asked**', '**can**' will be changed to '**could**',** second person **will be changed to** first person**.
 
• Therefore, all these conditions are satisfied by Option 4.

questions.question: Three persons A, B and C have different amount of rupees with them. If A gives 11 to C, A will have equal amount as B has. A and B together have total 245. How many rupees does B have?
questions.solution:
Let the total amount with B be Rs. X.

After giving to C, remaining amount with A = Total amount of A – 11 = X

Total amount of A = X + 11

Given, Total amount of A + Total amount of B = 245

It means, X + 11 + X = 245

2X = 245 – 11 = 234

X = 117

Total amount that B has is Rs. 117

Hence, “117” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some ants are bats.

Some ants are crabs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some bats are crabs.

II. No crab is ant.

III. No bat is crab.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
Either conclusion I or III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c467ed444f7b1a8f00d1f753baa0abeac71541feaf48eeb0f274f5ea6afa289.png] 

I. Some bats are crabs → False (it is possible but not definite).

II. No crab is ant → False (some ants are crabs)

III. No bat is crab → False (it is possible but not definite).

Here, I and III form a complementary pair.

Hence, “either conclusion I or III follows” is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(94, 44, 82)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Logic: **(1st number + 3rd number) ÷ 4 = 2nd number**.

Here, (94, 44, 82)

⇒ (94 + 82) ÷ 4

⇒ 176 ÷ 4 = 44.

Similarly, for **(48, 31, 76)**

**⇒ (48 + 76) ÷ 4**

questions.question: Three articles are bought at Rs. 200 each. One of them is sold at a loss of 10%. If the other two articles are sold so as to gain 20% on the whole transaction, then what is the gain percent on the two articles?

**Given:**

CP of 3 articles is Rs.200 each

Total gain percentage on whole transaction = 20%

**Calculation:**

Total CP of 3 articles = 200 × 3 = 600

So, SP of all three articles = 600 × 120/100 = 720

SP of 1st article = 200 – 200 × 10% = 180

CP of other 2 article = 400

SP of 2 other article = 720 – 180 = 540

Profit on 2 article = 540 – 400 = 140

Profit percentage of 2 article = (140/400) × 100 = 35%

**∴ The gain percent on the two articles is 35%**

questions.question: A can do 40% of a work in 6 days and B can do 30% of the same work in 3 days. They started the work together but B left after 2 days and A continued to work. In how many days was the entire work completed?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

A can do 40% of a work in 6 days

∴ A can do 100% of the work in 15 days

B can do 30% of the same work in 3 days

∴ B can do 100% of the same work in 10 days

Total work = LCM of (15 and 10) = 30

Efficiency of A = 30/15 = 2

Efficiency of B = 30/10 = 3

Work done by A and B together in 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10

Remaining work = 30 – 10 = 20

Remaining work done by A = 20/2 = 10 days

**∴ Total Number of days = 10 + 2 = 12 days**

questions.question: A train covers a certain distance in 45 minutes. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, it takes 3 minutes more to cover the same distance. The distance (in km) is:

 Base Rate

questions.question: Which of the following are flowerless plants that produce cones and seeds in which seeds are not encased within an ovary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is solution 4, i.e. Gymnosperms.

 
• **Gymnosperms** are the flowerless plant that produces **cones and seeds.**
 
• The term gymnosperm literally means "**naked seed**," as gymnosperm seeds are not encased within an ovary. Rather, they sit exposed on the surface of** leaf-like structures called bracts.**
 
• Gymnosperms are vascular plants of the sub kingdom Embyophyta and include **conifers, cycads, ginkgoes, and gnetophytes.**
 
• Some of the most recognizable examples of these woody shrubs and trees include** pines, spruces, firs, and ginkgoes.**
 
• Gymnosperms are abundant in **temperate forest** and** boreal forest biomes with species that can tolerate moist or dry conditions.**
 
• **Bryophyte**, the traditional name for **any nonvascular seedless plant**—namely,
 
 
• **mosses (division Bryophyta), **
 
• **hornworts (division Anthocerotophyta),**
 
• **liverworts (division Marchantiophyta). **
 
 
 
• Most **bryophytes lack complex tissue organization,** yet they show considerable diversity in form and ecology. They are widely distributed throughout the world and are relatively small compared with most seed-bearing plants.
 
• **Angiosperm**, any of about 300,000 species of **flowering plants, the largest and most diverse group within the kingdom Plantae. **Angiosperms represent approximately 80 per cent of all the known **green plants now living.** The angiosperms are** vascular seed plants in which the ovule (egg) is fertilized and develops into a seed in an enclosed hollow ovary. ** eg- Mango, Lemon etc.
 
• **Hydrophytes** are aquatic plants that are especially suited for living in aquatic environments. eg- Potamogeton crispus , Ceratophyllum and Hydrilla

questions.question: As of June 2019, who among the following is the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,i.e. N K Singh.

__
 
• **The Finance Commission** is a constitutional body, that determines the method and formula for distributing the tax proceeds between the Centre and states, and among the states as per the constitutional arrangement and present requirements.
 
• Under** Article 280 **of the Constitution, the President of India is required to constitute a Finance Commission at **an interval of five years or earlier.**
 
• The Finance Commission has** a chairman and four members appointed by the President.**
 
• In** November 2017**, President of India constituted **the 15th Finance Commission** and appointed former Planning Commission Member** N K Singh__ as its chairman.**
 
• **The First Finance Commission **was constituted under the chairmanship of **Shri K.C. Neogy on 6th April 1952.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a water borne disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,i.e. Mumps.

__
 
• **Mumps**__ is a **viral infection** that primarily affects **saliva-producing (salivary) glands that are located near ears.**
 
• Mumps can cause swelling in one or both of these glands.
 
• Mumps is an** airborne disease** and can be spread by an infected person coughing or sneezing and releasing tiny droplets of contaminated saliva, which can then be breathed in by another person.
 
• **Hepatitis, Cholera and Typhoid are waterborne diseases.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian Cricketer to hit a century in the very first session of a Test match?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Shikhar Dhawan**__ is an Indian Cricketer born in Delhi on Dec 5, 1985.
 
• He is a Left-handed batsman.
 
• Shikhar Dhawan shot to fame after an unprecedented run in the 2004 U-19 World Cup, where he scored 505 runs garnished with 3 hundreds.
 
• India vs Australia at Punjab Cricket Association IS Bindra Stadium, Mar 14, 2013, was his first Test debut.
 
• India vs Australia at Dr Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium, Oct 20, 2010, was his first ODI debut.
